english.title: Shine / direct laser beam towards a person providing air traffic services
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, shone or directed a laser beam towards a person providing air traffic services and the laser beam

(A)_[dazzled or distracted]_
(B)_[was likely to have dazzled or distracted]_

(C)_[that person]_
(D)_[another person providing air traffic services]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 2(1)(a)(ii), (4) and (5) of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Laser beam means a beam of coherent light produced by a device of any kind (section 3 of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018).
(ii) Air traffic services has the meaning given by section 98(1) of the Transport Act 2000.
(iii) It is a defence under this section to show that either they had a reasonable excuse, or, that they did not intend to shine or direct the laser beam towards the person and exercised all reasonable precautions to avoid doing so, see section 2(2) for details of this defence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 2(5) of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
